claim.statement: For six independent centered unit intervals grouped into three two-coordinate normalized banks and the symmetric Householder spectral matrix B=I-(2/3)11^T, the induced 6x6 physical A is entrywise nonzero with spectrum {1,1,-1,0,0,0}; its centered small-ball derivative I_* obeys the exact one-dimensional cone integral and the interval-certified lower bound I_*>4.0625, hence the output essential density norm exceeds 4.0625.

mathematical_premises: original physical coordinates X_i are independent Unif[-1/2,1/2] with density cap one
the three latent bank sums are independent only because their physical coordinate sets are disjoint
B=I-2nn^T with n=(1,1,1)/sqrt(3) is a Householder involution with spectrum {1,1,-1}
spherical coarea for this compact Lipschitz product density gives the centered small-ball derivative integral
the exact radial polynomial integral P(a) and the analytic Lipschitz constant 3sqrt(3)/2 give a deterministic midpoint error bound

partner_result_applied.actual_application: kappa=beta=a=1 gives A=[[1,1,-1],[1,1,1],[-1,1,1]], spectrum {2,2,-1}, and global arbitrary-cap-one bound ||p||_infinity<=2sqrt(2)<3sqrt(2)

remaining_implication: The fixed n=6 witness is below 3sqrt(2); no global orientation optimality is proved. The full theorem remains open. A sharp proof must aggregate grouped coordinates because every physical principal triple here is singular or has only half-scale spectrum.
next_step: Study exact symmetric Householder orientations for m>2 finite banks and whether their cone-tip values increase monotonically toward 3sqrt(2), while separately testing rough fragmented cap-one laws and off-zero modes.
